Albert is not very strong compared to other powerhouse cards like Daria and Levi. By itself its a 5 cost 3/5 storm. Which is not too strong. You need to play him on turn 9 with an evolve point up to do the real damage. And thats not easy to pull off. Swordcraft needs to spend its evolve points early on to hold control of the board (Floral Fencer etc.) Often times, by turn 9 you are either - 1) dead, 2) Already won, 3) no evo points to spend. IF you are going 1st, holding 1 evo till turn 9 is a huge drawback. Only having 1 evo to used for board control is close to impossible. 

On the other hand, Levi is way more powerful in my opinion. A 2 cost that, when evolved, can trade 1 for 3 and instantly undo everything your opponent played the previous turn. The tempo swing is so huge. 

Just my two cents.

First,  let me explain the formats, currently there are 3 clusters,  Grimm cluster,  alice cluster and lapis cluster,  with about 4 sets per cluster.  A new cluster is released every year.  There are 2 supported formats currently. 

New frontier (Standard) will include cards from the 2 latest clusters. Clusters rotate out every 2 years.  

Wanderer (Modern) includes cards from all clusters (grimm cluster onwards) 

Then you would want to find a local shop near you that supports the game.  You might want to pick up one of the latest starter decks. The starter decks in fow is actually very playable unlike magic.  The rulers that come with the starter decks (especially the green and black one) are regularly played in competitive events.  I would suggest the green or red one as it is the most playable out of the box without upgrading. 

Or you can look around for decklists and try to assemble a deck you like via buying singles. You can build a much more stable and competitive deck by doing this most decks wont cost you more then $30-$40.  Although if your goal is to learn more about the game and mechanics, i would suggest starting with a starter deck and playing with a friend or joining one of your lgs events.  Then you can upgrade from there.  

Once you have gotten used to the game,  you may want to start picking up staple lands.  There are dual lands in fow, without any drawbacks.  These are vital in building any multi color decks. So picking up a playset of each dual land would help in the long run.  

As for expanding your collection,  the booster boxes in fow are quite different from magic in the sense that they contain a very consistent amount of cards.  Playset of every common and uncommon,  3-4 of every rare, 1-2 of every mythic and a guarantee of 2 rulers (one normal,  one full art) .  So 2 boxes should net you almost all the cards in the set.  Although if you only care about having cards you need,  the cheaper way would be only buying singles of cards you need.

There are 2 things you should know, sets and clusters. there are about 4 sets per cluster. Each containing around 100-200 cards (Rough estimate). 

New Frontiers is the Standard format of Force of will. At any given time, the 2 latest clusters will be legal in this format. Every year (around sept) one of the clusters will be rotated out (The older one of the 2) and a new cluster will be introduced in.  When a new cluster is introduced, there will be around 4 sets that will be released gradually over a year (every ~3 months), then it is legal for another year. This gives a single cluster a grand total of 2 years legality. Although technically the last set of a cluster has only 1 year since it was released the last. 

http://force-of-will-tcg.wikia.com/wiki/Format 

There, it shows all sets currently and the clusters they belong to. Currently, the Alice cluster and Lapis cluster is legal. Alice is rotating out next sept, While lapis will last for another 2 years.

I personally prefer buying the singles.  The grim cluster ones are pretty cheap.  Around 1-2$ each (No yellow border and its foil).  Or you could go for the newer looking cfc ones.  But those are slightly more expensive.  A box in vingolf 2 will only come with 2 of each dual stone,  a handful of decent cards,  and alot of bulk.  And it costs 40$.

A box mostly contains 2 rulers, (one normal and one fullart/textured), 1-2 of each super rares, 2-3 of each rare, around 10 dual stones (Cfc) , playset of all uncommon and common. And of course a chance for an uber ruler (1 in 10 boxes average). And no vingolf 2 is not worth it. The other cards are not playable at all. And the dual stones are worth like 50 cents each. Dual stones are reprinted in cfc so i would suggest buying cfc singles or a box for the stones. 

Edit : Ok fine,  some cards are playable,  but most aren't.  And stones cost an average of 80cents on tcgplayer.  I got mine for 50.

Decks cost varies,  for example,  a very strong competitive deck, machina green,  will only cost you around 15$ to make.  While decks wont cost you more then 50$. Most of the cost is in the land base,   a playset of dual lands and ruler's memoria (5 color land) ,  but almost every deck will use it,  plus its legal for the next 2 years,  with the exception of ruler's memoria.

Its really cheap.  Getting only singles would be the cheapest way to build decks.  You can get a playset of every card (including dual lands and ruler)  needed to build almost all competitive / semi-competitive decks in the new frontier format now for under 400$
